request.spec:
A person can be retired from a date (defaults to the sheet's today). A claim dated after a
person's retirement date is refused with an error; claims dated on or before it are allowed even
if added later. Retired people are left out of the list (no row for them on the screen at all)
unless "show retired" is on: a toggle on the screen, off when the screen is first opened and left
as it is by loading a sheet. Their claims keep counting in every total. Show retired yes/no and
retired-from. Retiring writes PERSON_RETIRED name=<name> from=<date>.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A person can be retired from a date (defaults to the sheet's today). A claim dated after a
person's retirement date is refused with an error; claims dated on or before it are allowed even
if added later. Retired people are left out of the list (no row for them on the screen at all)
unless "show retired" is on: a toggle on the screen, off when the screen is first opened and left
as it is by loading a sheet. Their claims keep counting in every total. Show retired yes/no and
retired-from. Retiring writes PERSON_RETIRED name=<name> from=<date>.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
People can now be retired from a date, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**Stored data and server**
- A new migration, `V16__person_retired.sql`, adds a `retired_from` date to each person. It is empty for anyone not retired.
- A new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/retire`, retires a person from the date given, or from the sheet's today if no date is given. It writes `PERSON_RETIRED sheet=<id> by=<user> name=<name> from=<date>` to the audit file.
- Adding a claim dated after the person's retirement date is refused. Claims dated on or before it are still allowed, even if added later. A refused claim writes nothing to the store or the audit file. I also applied the same refusal when a draft claim is edited to a date after the retirement date; the request didn't ask for that, but it closes an obvious way around the rule.
- Retiring doesn't write a `ROLLUP` line, since no total changes; the expected audit lines in the test match this.

**Screen** (in `features/people/people.ts`)
- Each person's row shows retired yes/no and the retired-from date, plus a date box and a Retire button. A failed retire shows the row's `person-error`.
- A "Show retired" checkbox (`show-retired`) controls whether retired people appear. It is off when the screen first opens, and loading a sheet leaves it as it is. When it is off, retired people have no row at all.
- A retired person's claims still count in the claimed and due totals.

One side effect: retiring is saved like an edit, so it bumps the person's version. If someone else has that person open in the edit form at the time, their save will be refused as "someone else has saved this person".
